To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lipase is a useful marker for prostatic epithelia in the rat, that it is increased by progesterone, that it is decreased by estrogen and that it is not affected by thyroxine.
the distribution of lipase is different in the various lobes of the rat prostate, and that the activity of the lipase is influenced by the altered hormonal states.
the distribution of lipase in the prostatic acinar epithelial cells, interfollicular and periacinar stromal elements, blood vessels and mast cells is affected by the hormonal status of the animal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the histochemical demonstration of lipase activity and its distribution in the rat prostate.
the effect of hormones on the histochemical localization of lipase activity and its relation to the morphological features of the rat prostate.
the effects of altered hormonal states upon the histochemical distribution and activity of lipase in the rat prostate complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lipase activity is not a constant feature of the prostatic complex; it is affected by hormonal states.
the hormonal status has a profound influence on the histochemical pattern of lipase activity of all the lobes of the rat prostatic tissue.
the hormonal status of the rat prostatic glandular complex has a significant effect on lipase activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the enzyme is a useful marker for the effects of hormones on the prostatic complex.
lipase activity is increased in the rat ventral prostate when the hormonal milieu is altered in a manner to cause an increase in the size and number of the prostatic acini.
the histochemical distribution and activity of prostatic lipase are altered by changes in the hormonal status of the organism, and that these changes are not uniform throughout the prostatic complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lipase of the prostatic complex is under hormonal control, and that the pattern of distribution and intensity of activity is dependent upon the hormonal milieu of the animal.
the lipolytic enzyme is not a static entity, but one that responds to hormonal changes.
the lipase activity of prostatic tissue is subject to hormonal control and that this activity may be a useful index of the functional state of the prostatic complex in the rat.
